submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is the complement (off-state) of neuron L4/N2941's sparse detector: it rests at a low tonic level (peak ~0.17) on ordinary tokens that do not match the neuron's key, and is suppressed to ~0 exactly on tokens where the positive pole fires (e.g. ' carry', ' contain', ' pleaded', ' crossed' in context). Its peaks therefore mark the absence of the positive-pole trigger at the current token, not any positive content of their own; the exact tonic height wobbles by token identity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We left the mountain station before sunrise, and the narrow train wound down through pine forests into a valley stitched with orchards and slow brown rivers. At the first halt an old vendor sold roasted chestnuts wrapped in newspaper, and children pressed their faces to the glass as herons lifted off the marshes. The carriage smelled of oil and fresh bread, and a retired surveyor across the aisle unfolded a creased map to trace the route his grandfather had walked with mules and lanterns. By midday the hills flattened into wheat fields where windmills turned lazily and white farmhouses stood behind rows of poplars. We shared lunch with a botany student who named every weed along the embankment and pressed a sprig of thyme into our notebook for luck. In the afternoon the line followed the coast, and salt spray filmed the windows while fishing boats stitched white wakes into the blue bay and gulls screamed over the docks. A brass band was rehearsing in a seaside pavilion, and the tuba player waved at the train as it rattled past the promenade. Further on we crossed a viaduct above a gorge where swallows nested in the stonework and a waterfall threw rainbows over the ferns below. Evening found us in a market town with bells ringing from a tiled belfry, stalls piled with figs and olives, and drafts of cool air drifting down the alleys from the high pastures. We drank mint tea with a clockmaker who showed us gears no bigger than grains of rice and told stories of winters when wolves came down to the vineyards. Night fell as the train climbed again toward the plateau, stars thick above the silhouette of ruined watchtowers, and the conductor called the stops in a sleepy chant while passengers traded biscuits and blankets. At last the rails straightened toward the distant lights of the harbor city, and we gathered our bags and stepped onto the crowded platform
